_comment: MEMORA GOLD SET. Replace these examples with queries over YOUR real files. Target 20-30 rows. Rules: (1) write these BEFORE the retrieval pipeline exists, (2) each member writes queries against ANOTHER member's corpus so you aren't grading your own homework, (3) cover every 'type' below, (4) expected_sources are real filenames/ids in your test corpus. Delete this line before use.

notes: Zero content signal. Pure metadata. Dense-only retrieval MUST fail this - that failure is a result worth reporting.

query: what HR said during the internship interview
notes: Two-hop: resolve the phrase to a date window first, then search inside it.

query: the link someone shared about the hackathon last month
notes: Relative time + extract-a-link intent + informal source.

query: when did I last talk to Prof. Kulkarni about the project
notes: Same person as 'a.kulkarni@college.edu' and 'AK'. Entity normalization required.

query: summarize what I learned about vector databases
notes: The easy case. Dense retrieval alone should handle this. Baseline sanity check.
Never stored. System must say it doesn't have this, not answer from model knowledge. Grade as PASS only on refusal.

query: the handwritten notes I photographed before the viva
notes: Tests OCR quality on handwriting AND temporal resolution together.

query: which files mention the Memora architecture
notes: Multi-source recall test. Recall@k matters more than precision here.
